messages.content: What were the stock prices of Apple Inc. listed on NASDAQ and Microsoft Corporation listed on NYSE for the past 10 and 15 days respectively?

function.name: get_stock_price
function.description: Retrieve the stock price for a specific company and time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

company.description: The ticker symbol of the company.

They want stock prices for Apple (NASDAQ) for past 10 days, and Microsoft (NYSE) for past 15 days. We have a function get_stock_price that can retrieve stock price for a specific company and time frame. The function signature: get_stock_price({company: string, days: number, exchange?: string}). The user wants Apple on NASDAQ, 10 days; Microsoft on NYSE, 15 days. So we need to call the function twice. But the function returns "any" - presumably a list of prices. We need to call it twice. Probably ticker symbol. The user says "Apple Inc. listed on NASDAQ". So we can use ticker "AAPL" and exchange "NASDAQ". For Microsoft, ticker "MSFT" and exchange "NYSE". But Microsoft is actually listed on NASDAQ too. But user says NYSE. We'll follow user. So call get_stock_price for Apple: {company: "AAPL", days: 10, exchange: "NASDAQ"}. For Microsoft: {company: "MSFT", days: 15, exchange: "NYSE"}.

We need to output the results. We'll call the function twice.
